name: Grand Palace and Wat Phra Kaeo
blurb: Royal palace complex that holds Wat Phra Kaeo and the Emerald Buddha; the must-see sight in central Bangkok.
priceText: 500 baht for foreigners, incl. Wat Phra Kaeo and Queen Sirikit Museum of Textile; Thai citizens free with ID card
when: Daily 08:30–15:30 (tickets sold until 15:30; site footer says 16:30)

name: Wat Rakhang (Temple of the Bells)
blurb: Thonburi temple named the Temple of the Bells after a huge bell found there; the visit is free.

name: National Museum Bangkok
blurb: Bangkok's national museum in the old Front Palace grounds; attractive in parts but sprawling, so pick what you want to see.
priceText: 200 baht for foreigners; 30 baht for Thais

name: Bangkok Art and Culture Centre (BACC)
blurb: Free art centre in Siam Square with interactive exhibits and temporary shows across performance, music, painting and film.

name: Roti-Mataba
blurb: Popular Thai-Muslim eatery near Khao San with roti, mataba stuffed pancakes and massaman curry; sit downstairs for the local feel.

name: Krua Apsorn
blurb: Unpretentious Dusit restaurant with authentic traditional Thai cooking; it won a Bangkok Post best-restaurant contest in 2006.

name: Overtone Music Cave
blurb: Live-music bar on Royal City Avenue where every seat faces the stage; jazz, rock and blues, with the focus on listening.

name: Brick Bar
blurb: Underground ska and reggae bar on Khao San with live bands and an old-style Western interior; packed at weekends, and IDs are checked.

name: Shewa Spa
blurb: A bit pricier than the nearby parlours but cleaner and more professional, with well-trained staff for Thai, oil and herbal massage.

name: Follow Me Bicycle Tours
blurb: Half-day bike ride through Bangkok's residential streets; a fish spa and a barbecue meal come with the price.

name: Batu Caves
blurb: Limestone caves used as Hindu temples since their discovery in 1878, just outside the city centre; visiting is free.

name: Petronas Twin Towers
blurb: Iconic twin towers: the Skybridge at levels 41–42, then the observation deck at level 86 for panoramic city views.
priceText: Foreigners: adult RM80, child RM30; Malaysians: adult RM25, child RM12

name: Sultan Abdul Samad Building
blurb: 1897 colonial government building fronting Merdeka Square, built by British architects; a free landmark stop.

name: Seri Negara
blurb: Restored colonial mansion that reopened in December 2025 as a cultural museum on Malaysia's road to nationhood.

name: Islamic Arts Museum Malaysia
blurb: One of KL's best museums: Malaysian art and objects set within the wider Islamic world, with religious and aesthetic pieces.
priceText: RM14 (Wikivoyage; official site shows no prices)

name: National Museum (Muzium Negara)
blurb: Malaysia's national museum: traditional life of its ethnic groups, shadow puppets, Orang Asli woodcarvings and national history.

name: Soong Kee Beef Noodles
blurb: Beef noodle shop said to date from 1945; dry noodles with beef mince, with the beef balls served separately in soup.

name: Zouk Kuala Lumpur
blurb: KL branch of the Singapore club, playing house and dance music, especially on Fridays; the listing advises dressing well in black.
priceText: RM40 for men, RM30 for women (incl. one drink); drinks from RM25

name: Stroll around Kampung Baru
blurb: Unspoilt Malay quarter a stone's throw from the skyscrapers; one of the city's most fascinating neighbourhoods.

name: KL Forest Eco Park
blurb: Last primary tropical rainforest inside Kuala Lumpur; birds, monkeys and lizards can show up along the paths.
priceText: Foreigners: adult RM40, child (6–16) RM5; Malaysians: RM10 / RM1

name: Gardens by the Bay
blurb: Free outdoor gardens and Supertree Grove on Marina Bay; the Flower Dome and Cloud Forest domes cost extra and open until 9pm.
priceText: Outdoor gardens free; Flower Dome S$30 (incl. Supertree Observatory); both domes S$53; OCBC Skyway S$5/3

name: Singapore City Gallery
blurb: URA gallery with large scale models of the whole country and the city centre; the best free orientation for first-timers.

name: Changi Chapel and Museum
blurb: Memorial to the WWII Japanese POW camp that is the setting of King Rat; a replica of the original chapel stands on a new site.

name: Reflections at Bukit Chandu
blurb: Small, well-made museum on the Malay Regiment's last stand in WWII's Battle of Bukit Chandu; the building once housed an opium factory.

name: Asian Civilisations Museum
blurb: Asia-wide collection in the historic Empress Place building; one of Singapore's largest and best-presented museums.
priceText: $25 for foreign adults; $20 concession for students with valid ID (passport or school pass); official admissions page, figures shown for a special exhibition

name: Tian Tian Hainanese Chicken Rice
blurb: Chinatown stall that the New York Times called a chicken rice shrine; expect a long queue, and it often sells out early.
when: Tue–Sun 11:00–20:00 in theory; often sells out early

name: MacRitchie Reservoir and Treetop Walk
blurb: Jungle-fringed reservoir with the 250 m HSBC Treetop Walk, suspended as high as 27 m; a free day out.

name: Bukit Timah Nature Reserve
blurb: Singapore's highest point at 166 m and one of its last patches of original primary tropical rainforest; free to visit.

name: Rumours Beach Club
blurb: Sentosa beach bar with free entry and pleasant outdoor seating; reserve a pavilion in advance, and expect the music to be loud.

name: Kwan Im Thong Hood Cho temple
blurb: Singapore's most popular Buddhist temple, dedicated to Kuan Yin; wish-makers keep it packed, so expect crowds.

name: Meiji Jingu shrine
blurb: Tokyo's grandest Shinto shrine in Harajuku, built in 1920 to commemorate Emperor Meiji; entry to the shrine is free.

name: Sensō-ji temple, Asakusa
blurb: Asakusa's main temple; the main hall opens early and closes at 17:00, so an early start works well.
when: Main hall 06:30–17:00 Oct–Mar, 06:00–17:00 other months; grounds hours not listed

name: National Museum of Western Art
blurb: Western art, including the original Rodin The Thinker, in a Le Corbusier building that is on the UNESCO World Heritage list.
priceText: ¥500 adult; ¥250 university or college student (permanent collection)

name: Edo-Tokyo Museum
blurb: Striking building raised above the ground to resemble an old warehouse, covering Tokyo's history from 1590; a long, rich visit.
priceText: Adult ¥1,300; university student with ID ¥1,040; younger students with ID free (Wikivoyage)

name: Asakura Museum of Sculpture
blurb: Sculptor Asakura Fumio's house and studio in Taito, with a garden and a vaulted studio hall; small and atmospheric.
priceText: Adult ¥500, student ¥250 (Wikivoyage; ID rule not stated)

name: Tsukiji Outer Market
blurb: Food-shop lanes that stayed behind when the wholesale fish market moved to Toyosu in 2018.
when: Mon–Sat about 09:00–14:00 (varies by shop); closed most Wednesdays and holidays

name: Kagetsudo
blurb: Melon pan bakery making its buttery, crisp-topped cakes since 1945, with the decor unchanged; a cheap snack stop.

name: Abbott's Choice
blurb: Small Roppongi bar with NYC pop on the radio and a mix of tourists, expats and locals; a respite from pricier bars nearby.

name: Hair of the Dogs
blurb: Punk-rock bar in Shinjuku with a Mexican wrestler theme; the cover buys a bar seat, and you pick the music from a menu.
priceText: ¥800 to sit at the bar (cover); drinks average ¥700

name: Ōi Racecourse
blurb: Major horse-racing track with night racing from March to December and a Grade I race in December; cheap entry and food stalls.
when: Night races March–December; daily hours not listed

name: Gyeongbokgung Palace
blurb: Seoul's grandest Joseon palace, razed by a Japanese invasion in 1592 and later rebuilt; a must-see on any palace route.
priceText: ₩3,000 (Wikivoyage; youth and other rates not verified)
when: Closed Tue; opens 09:00, closes 17:00–18:30 by season

name: Changdeokgung Palace
blurb: UNESCO palace built in 1405 and a seat of power until 1896; restored halls in an elegant setting.

name: National Museum of Korea
blurb: Korea's flagship national museum; the permanent exhibitions are free, and only the special exhibitions cost money.
priceText: Free for permanent exhibitions; special exhibitions paid (official site)
when: Mon, Tue, Thu, Fri, Sun 09:30–17:30; Wed & Sat 09:30–21:00

name: MMCA Seoul (National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art)
blurb: Korean modern and contemporary art on a former military hospital site; free for visitors under 24 and on the last Wednesday monthly.
priceText: ₩4,000 standard (Wikivoyage; official site says fees vary by exhibition); free for under 24 or over 65, undergraduates with ID, and the last Wednesday of each month
when: Mon, Tue, Thu, Fri, Sun 10:00–18:00; Wed & Sat 10:00–21:00

name: National Palace Museum of Korea
blurb: Free national museum of royal palace artefacts, open later on Wednesdays and Saturdays.

name: Bakgane Bindaetteok Main Branch
blurb: Gwangjang Market's mung-bean pancake specialist, grinding beans on a millstone for a crisp, savoury bindaetteok.

name: Lotte World Ice Rink
blurb: Indoor rink on the first floor of Lotte World that you can use without riding the theme park; a good winter treat.
priceText: ₩13,000 (Wikivoyage); a ₩19,000 set option is also listed

name: Sparex 24 jjimjilbang
blurb: Round-the-clock Korean bathhouse across two mall basements, with separate men's and women's baths and a food court.

name: Radiohead pub (Songpa)
blurb: Songpa pub with five draft beers picked by a bartending-contest winner, a wine and spirits list, and song requests.

name: Yeouido Hangang Park
blurb: One of Seoul's busiest riverside parks: wide lawns, bike hire nearby and Han River sunsets; free to enter.

name: Independence Palace (Reunification Palace)
blurb: Former South Vietnamese presidential palace kept much as it was when Saigon fell in 1975; a 1960s time warp.
priceText: 80,000 VND adult; 40,000 VND students and seniors (conditions not stated); children 6–16 20,000 (official site)

name: Quan Am Pagoda
blurb: Oldest pagoda in town, dedicated to Quan Am and built by Hokkien immigrants; lots of incense and a cheerful resident puppy.

name: War Remnants Museum
blurb: Opened within months of Saigon's fall, with US tanks, jets and helicopters plus three floors of exhibits; sobering, so allow time.

name: Museum of Vietnamese History
blurb: Fine collection of Vietnamese antiquities; read up on the history first. The botanical gardens outside make a cheap lunch spot.

name: Southern Women's Museum
blurb: Often-overlooked museum on women's roles in the south's society, economy and revolutionary history, shown in photos and documents.

name: Ben Thanh Market
blurb: Touristy central market, easy to spot by its clock tower; the pho stalls inside are the real deal.

name: Pho Quynh
blurb: Pho specialist near Ben Thanh, open 24 hours, with air-conditioned upper floors and a decent beef-stew banh mi.

name: Quan An Ngon
blurb: Vietnamese dishes served in atmospheric old French villas; two branches share the name, one on Pasteur Street.

name: Khong Ten
blurb: Big cabaret with Vietnamese celebrity singers that locals know from TV; mellow music that many visitors find an acquired taste.

name: Dam Sen Water Park
blurb: Water park close to the centre with unusual slides such as the 'Space Bowl', a restaurant and animatronic dinosaurs.
priceText: 40,000–110,000 VND by height and arrival time; 90,000 VND after 16:00; under 0.8 m free

name: Palace of Knossos
blurb: Crete's best-known Minoan palace; compact enough to cover the main areas in about 30 minutes, and much of it is accessible.
priceText: Full €15, concessions €8 (Wikivoyage; ministry site unreachable; a 2026 guide says €20, unverified)

name: Heraklion Archaeological Museum
blurb: Crete's top museum for Minoan finds: Snake Goddess statues, the Bull-Leaping Fresco, the Phaistos Disk and Minoan seals.
priceText: Full €12, concessions €6; €20 combined with Knossos (valid 3 days) (Wikivoyage; site unreachable)

name: Historical Museum of Crete
blurb: Crete's story from Byzantine times to today, including material on WWII and the German occupation.
priceText: Adults €8; €5 concession for pupils and students on ID, and senior citizens; children 12 and under free (official site)

name: Natural History Museum of Crete
blurb: Natural environment of the Eastern Mediterranean with a focus on Greece and Crete; an indoor option for a cloudy day.

name: Koules fortress
blurb: 16th-century Venetian harbour fort; the parapet looks across to Dia Islet, where Cousteau found sunken Cretan trade remains.

name: Fortifications of Heraklion
blurb: Massive 15th–17th-century Venetian walls and bastions around the old city; a walkable route through the centre.

name: CretAquarium Thalassokosmos
blurb: Largest aquarium in the Eastern Mediterranean, with sharks in its big tank; winter hours end at 16:00, so plan early.

name: Avli
blurb: Courtyard meze spot down an alley; the menu is Greek only, but the owner's daughter speaks English and helps you order.

name: Pagopiion (Ice Factory)
blurb: Quirky restaurant and bar on St Titus Square with dramatic decor and outdoor seats by the church; the food is praised.

name: Kafeneio O Ntokos
blurb: Tiny traditional kafeneio next to the fish market, where mezedes go with beer or raki; a local drinking spot.
